findings.title: A hold set by a failing command fires no waiting-on-human hook
quotes: fire the events `step-passed`, `step-skipped`, `gate-approved`, `gate-rejected`, `epic-closed`, `waiting-on-human` and `effort-done`
return 1, talk(slug, stopped(here, stop, slug) if stop else here)
if result[0] == 0:
findings.fix: fire `after` whenever the history grew or the hold changed, whatever the exit code. Alternatively, have the stop path return 0, or state in the spec that the event fires only from successful commands.

sources.situation: an auto effort hits a stop-list rule in `_done`. The code writes the pause line with `write(root, slug, [line], new, w, here["stage"])` and returns code 1, so `hooked` skips `extensions.after`. The effort is now waiting for the human, but the notify hook registered on `waiting-on-human` never runs and nothing is recorded. The silent case is the one the event exists for. The same applies to any other command that sets a hold and exits 1.

findings.reason: flow.py `hooked` calls `extensions.after` only when `result[0] == 0`, and the `_done` stop-list path writes the pause line then returns `1, talk(...)`, so no waiting-on-human fires for that hold.

findings.title: `nio extensions add` runs a command from the source argument, which breaks "runs none of its commands"
quotes: run none of its commands and print every check and hook command it brings
code, _, err = records.git(tmp, "clone", "--depth", "1", source, tmp + "/c", full=True)
findings.fix: refuse a source that starts with `-`, and pass `--` before it in the clone call.

sources.situation: a source is routed to `git clone` when it contains `://`, starts with `git@` or ends with `.git`. It is passed to git as a bare argument with no `--`. A string like `--upload-pack=<cmd> ://x.git` is read by git as an option, so `<cmd>` runs at add time. That includes a command copied from a README line "nio extensions add ...". Extensions come from third parties, so the add is the trust boundary FR-37 protects.

findings.reason: extensions.py line 263 passes `tmp + "/c"` as the next positional, so an option-shaped source swallows no repository. The positional left is the nonexistent local path, so git fails before running any upload-pack command. Missing `--` is hygiene, not the described command execution.

findings.title: A step name is not validated, so a step can be unreachable or silently replaced
quotes: lacks a required field
name must be a word of letters, digits, - and _
findings.fix: validate step names with NAME, and refuse a name that repeats within a manifest.

sources.situation: only the extension name is checked against NAME. A step `name` need only be a non-empty string. A step named `run e2e` or `a.b` becomes a stage that `stage_arg` rejects, so `nio flow done` can never pass it. An effort reaching it is stuck, and `remove` refuses while an effort sits there. Two steps with the same name in one manifest pass `check`. `table` keys on `<ext>.<step>`, so the second silently replaces the first, and the first check never runs. A step named `s.jury` also collides with the jury stage of step `s`.

findings.reason: `check` only requires step `name` to be a non-empty string (lines 76-80). NAME is applied to the extension name only (line 61). The duplicate-step test at line 146 compares against other extensions, never within `own`, so same-named steps pass and `table` keys collide.

findings.title: A project folder named like a shipped extension shadows it
quotes: WHEN `nio extensions add` is given the name of a shipped extension THE SYSTEM SHALL copy the shipped extension
if Path(source).is_dir():
findings.fix: resolve a bare word, one with no `/`, as a name first, and a path only when it has a separator or `./`. Alternatively, refuse when both exist.

sources.situation: `resolve` tries a directory at the relative path first. A Playwright project usually has its own `e2e/` folder, so `nio extensions add e2e` in the exact project that wants the shipped e2e extension resolves to `./e2e`. The result is the refusal "manifest.json is missing", or worse, a user folder that happens to hold a manifest is added with the source label `e2e`. The shipped extension is unreachable by name there.

findings.title: A hook's timeout has no upper bound, so a failing or slow hook can block the flow
quotes: a failing hook never stops or blocks the flow
timeout must be a whole number of seconds of at least 1
ponytail: a hook line is written under its own short lock, one per hook; batch them if hooks get many.
findings.fix: cap the per-hook timeout and the total hook time per command. Document that hooks block for up to that time, or run them detached.

sources.situation: hooks run in the foreground inside `nio flow done`, one after another, for every event. Each defaults to 300 seconds and the manifest can set any integer. One command can fire `gate-approved`, `step-passed` and `effort-done`, and each of those can fire several hooks. A hook that hangs (a network call, say) holds the command for hours, and the human or the driver sees a hung flow command. The `after` hook run also reads the history window `lines[n:]`. A concurrent command's lines can therefore fire the same event twice.

findings.title: Three e2e ACs have only tests that were skipped
quotes: skipped test_app_started_and_stopped (set NIO_E2E=1)
skipped test_failure_keeps_trace_and_screenshot (set NIO_E2E=1)
skipped test_tester_writes_one_test_per_e2e_ac (set NIO_E2E=1)
findings.fix: run them with NIO_E2E=1, Playwright, Chromium and a model, and put the passing results in the evidence; or the human accepts these three ACs as unproven.

sources.situation: AC-29 (the tester writes one test per e2e AC), AC-34 (the app is started and stopped around the run) and AC-35 (trace and screenshots are kept) are covered only by tests/test_extensions_e2e.py. In the evidence run all three printed skip and the pack lists them as failed. There is no passing result for any of the three. TC-29 also calls `check.py` directly, not `nio flow done e2e.tests`.

test_tester_writes_one_test_per_e2e_ac, test_app_started_and_stopped and test_failure_keeps_trace_and_screenshot (tests/test_extensions_e2e.py:77, 41, 59) are the only tests for these ACs and each is reported as failed. The file's header says they run only with NIO_E2E and otherwise print skipped and pass, so these results most likely come from an environment problem (npm install, Chromium, or the claude model). The cause is not visible in the pack. As it stands, the Playwright webServer start and stop (FR-32), the trace and screenshots (FR-33) and the tester writing the tests (FR-29) have no passing evidence.

`uv run python tests/test_extensions.py` or `NIO_E2E=1 uv run python tests/test_extensions_e2e.py` is run. Importing `test_extensions` reaches its module-level `selfcheck.main(...)` (test_extensions.py:917), which runs test_extensions' 49 tests labelled as test_extensions_e2e.py and calls sys.exit. `test_app_started_and_stopped`, `test_failure_keeps_trace_and_screenshot` and `test_tester_writes_one_test_per_e2e_ac` never execute, yet the file can exit 0. The run's output shows "ran 49 tests, 0 failed" for test_extensions_e2e.py, with none of the e2e tests in it.

findings.reason: tests/test_extensions.py:917 calls `selfcheck.main(...)` unguarded, and `selfcheck.main` ends in `sys.exit`. tests/test_extensions_e2e.py imports `from test_extensions import ...` at line 15, so the import runs the whole suite and exits before any `@e2e` test is defined or run. The three e2e tests can never execute, with or without NIO_E2E.

findings.fix: make the unchanged-tests check not depend on a `main` ref in the copy, for example by comparing a recorded hash of the expected stage table, or by running it where `main` exists. Then re-collect.

The test now checks `flow.table` identity, runs test_flow.py, and looks for the new test's name in the file text (line 249, "no `main` ref needed"). findings.title: The hook line records the effort's stage, not the event's stage
quotes: from": stage, "to": stage
findings.fix: decide which stage the line carries. If it is the event's stage, write `from`/`to` from the `stage` argument in `fire`. If it is the effort's stage, change CT-11's shape and the `fire` docstring to say so and drop the `stage` argument's use for the record.

sources.situation: an extension step `e2e.tests` passes. `extensions.after` calls `fire(root, slug, "step-passed", f, ...)` with `f` = `e2e.tests`, so the event's stage is the step. Inside `fire`, `here = flow.last_to(lines)` (`src/nio/extensions.py` line 381) is the stage the flow moved to, `tasking`, and the `hook` line is written with `from` and `to` set to `tasking`. CT-11 says the line is `{"from": stage, "to": stage, ...}` with `stage` the event's stage, so the line should read `e2e.tests`. The effort's timeline (FR-18, CT-6) then puts the hook at the wrong stage. The `stage` argument is also passed to `NIO_STAGE`, so the hook's env and its record disagree.

CT-11 writes the hook line as from: stage, to: stage with the event's stage. fire() ignores its `stage` argument for the line, using the effort's current stage. After step-passed for plan_jury the line says the effort is at e2e.tests, and a gate-rejected line names the step it was sent back to. A reader cannot tell which stage the hook fired for, since NIO_STAGE is not stored. The code's choice is plausible (a line with from not equal to to might move where()), but it departs from the contract and no test pins it.

findings.reason: contracts.md line 110 says the hook line is `{"from": stage, "to": stage, ...}`. `fire` ignores `stage` for the record and writes `here = flow.last_to(lines)` into from/to (extensions.py lines 381-384), so the contract and the code differ.

findings.title: A task's e2e test check is not limited to full specs
quotes: on a full spec, a task whose `Serves:` holds an AC at `Level: e2e` (CT-17) must cite in `Test:` a TC aimed at that AC
if full and "Test" in f and not ids(f["Test"]):
findings.fix: wrap the new check in `if full and ...`, as the `Test:` check beside it is, or amend CT-12 if the error is meant for lite specs too.

sources.situation: CT-12 applies only on a full spec. In `src/nio/tasks.py` the new `errs += [f"{t} serves {ac} (Level: e2e) ..."]` line sits outside any `full` test, while the neighbouring `Test:` check is `if full and ...`. On a lite spec, `aimed` stays `{}` (it is built only when `full`), so a task serving an AC whose own `Level:` is `e2e` and whose `Test:` names no TC gets the error, which CT-12 does not allow. Reachability depends on whether a lite spec can carry `Level: e2e`, which I did not confirm.

findings.title: nio fails to import on Python 3.11
quotes: {join([f'{m['name']}.{s['name']} (after {s['after']})' for s in m['steps']], ', ')}
findings.fix: build the step, card and hook strings before the f-string, or use different quote characters, so the file parses on 3.11; or raise requires-python to 3.12.

sources.situation: pyproject.toml says requires-python >=3.11, but listing() reuses the same quote inside an f-string, which is only legal from Python 3.12. On 3.11 extensions.py is a SyntaxError. cli.py imports it at the top, so every nio command fails, not only `nio extensions list`.

findings.reason: extensions.py lines 340 and 342 nest `f'{m['name']}...'` inside an f-string using the same single quote, which parses only from Python 3.12 (PEP 701). pyproject.toml says `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, and cli.py line 9 imports extensions at the top, so 3.11 fails every nio command.

findings.title: `nio extensions remove` deletes whatever path the name resolves to
quotes: rec, d = read_record(root), folder(root) / name
findings.fix: refuse a name that is not a plain extension name (no slash, not starting with a dot) before touching the filesystem. Also require `name in rec` or a real folder directly under .nio/extensions.

sources.situation: the name is never checked against the extension name pattern. `nio extensions remove .` gives d = .nio/extensions, which is a directory, so the "not added" refusal is skipped. `sitting` and `followers` find nothing, then `shutil.rmtree(d)` wipes every extension and the record. `..` gives .nio, so the same call would wipe the whole .nio folder.

findings.reason: `remove` never matches `name` against NAME and cli.py passes `a.name` straight through. With `.`, `d` is `.nio/extensions`, which is a directory, so the not-added refusal is skipped. `sitting` and `followers` find nothing, and line 360 runs `shutil.rmtree(d)`.

findings.title: The run report leaves out extension gate approvals
quotes: each gate's approval (under auto, with its grant line)
findings.fix: read the gates from table(root, False)[1] in report.

sources.situation: under auto the pull-request body is flow.report, which lists each gate's approval and its grant line. It loops over the built-in GATES, so an approved or auto-approved extension gate (for example e2e.tests.jury) never appears. The human reviewing the PR does not see that the flow approved it under auto. The GATES lookups in report should have moved to table(root) with the other readers.

findings.title: Self-check depends on a local main ref
quotes: def test_no_extensions_changes_nothing():
findings.fix: drop the git-diff assertions, or make them skip when main is missing; keep the table identity check and the test_flow.py run.

sources.situation: this test asserts that the diff of tests/test_flow.py against `main` has only added lines and holds test_status_speed_with_three_extensions. In a copy with no main ref, or once the branch is merged, the diff is empty or errors, the any(...) is false and the test fails (as the evidence run in a throwaway copy showed). The check is about the repo's history, not about the code, so it breaks on any checkout that is not this branch. The identity assert on flow.table above it already covers the no-extension case of CT-6.

findings.title: The run report ignores extension jury gates
quotes: if x["kind"] in ("pass", "override") and x["from"] in GATES:
findings.fix: in `report`, use `table(root, False)[1]` in both loops, the same table `used` already reads.

sources.situation: an effort with an extension step that declares a jury gate (for example `ext.step.jury`) is approved. `flow.used` and `stops` count that gate through `table(root)[1]`. `flow.report`, the run report and the PR body under auto, still loops only over the built-in `GATES`. The gate's approval, accepted risks and fixes never appear in the report.

findings.title: The new `nio extensions` command and its tests are named in no doc
quotes: add, list or remove extensions: folders that add steps, cards and hooks
findings.fix: add one README row for `nio extensions add|list|remove` and the two test commands to the CLAUDE.md list.

sources.situation: the diff adds the `nio extensions` command (the help text quoted above), but the README command table (the `nio agents sync|verify` row) and the CLAUDE.md self-check list were not touched. Neither lists `nio extensions add|list|remove`, `tests/test_extensions.py` or `NIO_E2E=1 tests/test_extensions_e2e.py`. A maintainer or agent following those docs does not learn the command or the checks exist. No skill mentions extensions either.

findings.title: The e2e check re-implements the AC-level rule that `spec.level` now holds
quotes: found = re.findall(r"Level:\s*([a-z0-9]+)", block[max(block.find("Observable:"), 0):])
findings.fix: leave the copy and add a test asserting `e2e_acs` and `spec.level` agree on the same blocks, or accept the duplication as deliberate and comment it in `check.py`.

sources.situation: CT-17 introduced `spec.level` so `plan.py` and `tasks.py` agree on an AC's own level. `src/nio/shipped/e2e/check.py::e2e_acs` repeats the same regex and slicing. It does the same job for the e2e step's AC selection. `tests_of` also repeats the `### TC-n ... (AC-n; level)` heading parse that `tasks.py` does. If the rule changes, the e2e step silently disagrees with `nio check tasks`. The extension is stdlib-only by design, which explains a copy, but nothing ties the two together.

findings.title: `flow.moves` keeps a built-in-only branch nothing reaches

quotes: FAIL tests/test_extensions.py::test_timeouts_stop_commands
findings.fix: make the no-leftover check specific to this test's own commands (a unique marker per run or per root), or stop the e2e file from re-running the whole of test_extensions. Then re-collect.

sources.situation: the evidence run records the AC-47 test failed, because `pgrep` found `sleep 60 # nio-t-hook` still running. The suite runs test_extensions.py and test_extensions_e2e.py in parallel, and the second file re-runs the same tests. The `pgrep` pattern is machine-wide, so one process sees the other's live sleep. The T-30/T-31 round changed this test from `sleep 5` to `sleep 60`, which widens the overlap.

findings.reason: tests/test_extensions.py:711 runs `pgrep -af "^/bin/sh -c sleep 60 # nio-t-"`, which matches every process on the machine and has no per-run marker. test_extensions_e2e.py re-runs the whole suite through its import (see J-14), and the suite files run in parallel (`xargs -P8`). A concurrent copy's live `sleep 60 # nio-t-hook` therefore makes `returncode == 1` fail.
